newsitem.title: FRANCE: Rain disrupts start of French rapeseed harvest.
newsitem.headline: Rain disrupts start of French rapeseed harvest.

text.p: Rain has slowed the rapeseed harvest in France's southwest and pushed back the start of operations in other regions, crop experts said on Wednesday.
Warm temperatures in April helped speed up crop development but wet weather since the middle of the month now threatens to cancel that advantage, they said.
"The crop was two weeks ahead of schedule, now it is losing its advance," oilseeds analyst Bernard Nicol said.
In the southwest the first cuts started in early June but the rain has slowed down combining operations and harvesting is now only two-thirds complete.
But in the main producing area of central France and Burgundy and Franche-Comte in the east, the rain has delayed the start of harvesting operations.
"The harvest may begin within two weeks, provided there is a break in the weather," an analyst from the French oilseeds research institute Cetiom said.
In the southwest, initial data from the fields are confirming initial fears the crop suffered from a prolonged spring drought.
Crop analysts now predict regional yields may fall to 2.5-2.6 tonnes per hectare from a record 3.1 tonnes last year.
But they stressed the local area sown to rapeseed is only a marginal 100,000 hectares.
In other regions substantial rain since May should allow the crop to recoup some of its losses but analysts said it was premature to make any predictions.
"At this stage it is safe to stick to the most recent estimates made by the French farm ministry," the Cetiom analyst said.
In its June report the ministry forecast the national 1997 winter rapeseed yield may fall to 2.94 tonnes from 3.33 percent in 1996, mostly the result of dry weather in March and April.
Assuming a 9.5 percent rise in 1997 winter rapesed sowings to 941,000 hectares, the ministry forecast a 3.3 percent fall in the winter rapeseed crop to 2.767 million tonnes.
